short: Four Japanese fleet carriers lost in a single morning, and the Pacific war turned.
full:
Yamamoto's plan was to seize Midway atoll and destroy the American carriers when they came out to defend it. American cryptanalysts had broken enough of the Japanese naval code to identify both the target and the date, so Nimitz stationed three carriers north-east of the island in ambush rather than sailing into the trap.

On the morning of 4 June 1942 American torpedo bombers attacked without fighter escort and were almost annihilated without scoring a hit, but they drew the Japanese combat air patrol down to sea level. Dive bombers arriving overhead minutes later found Akagi, Kaga and Soryu with fuelled and armed aircraft on their decks; all three were fatally hit within about six minutes. Hiryu was caught that afternoon after crippling Yorktown, which was finished off by a submarine on the 7th. Japan lost four fleet carriers and a core of irreplaceable aircrew, and never mounted another strategic offensive in the Pacific.
